risk_if_not_implemented: Without Contingency Plan Testing & Exercises, critical business processes and services may not withstand or recover from disruption, causing extended outages and data loss. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), Recovery Failure / Unacceptable Recovery Delay (R-OR-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Contingency Plan Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and "lessons learned" activity every time the contingency plan is activated.
compensating_control_1.justification: Contingency Plan Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned (BCD-11) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Contingency Plan Testing & Exercises (BCD-10) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Data Backups
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to create recurring backups of data, software and/or system images, as well as verify the integrity of these backups, to ensure the availability of the data to satisfy Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs).
compensating_control_2.justification: Data Backups (BCD-24) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Contingency Plan Testing & Exercises (BCD-10) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
